title: Model-Fit Field Labs — rapid A/B probes for latency tolerance & fallback economics
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Objective: Run 4 rapid, low-friction 'field lab' experiments with partner customers to quantify (1) how much end-to-end latency customers tolerate before experience or conversions degrade, and (2) the economic tradeoffs when applying fallback policies (cheaper quantized models, increased batching, or regional reroutes).

Why now: We have strong internal benchmarks for token/microsecond economics, but limited signal about real product-level tolerance curves (e.g., search UI CTR, chat session continuation, internal enterprise workflows). Concrete customer-facing datasets will directly inform (a) default routing and fallback policies in Smart Routing, (b) pricing buckets for Dedicated customers, and (c) RBAC/contract triggers for SLA/penalty clauses.

Success metrics (end of field-labs):
- Per-customer latency tolerance curve (90th/95th quantiles) mapped to business metrics (CTR, completion rate) in three discrete workload profiles.
- Measured cost delta and quality delta for each fallback policy (quantized model variant, smaller architecture, caching bias).
- Recommended policy matrix (per-workload) with confidence band and recommended default for Redwood Optimize and Smart Routing engine.

Approach:
1) Define 3 workload cohorts (support chat, semantic search, batch re-ranking) and instrument minimal telemetry.
2) Draft lightweight A/B probe runner integrated with hosted API to (a) inject controlled latency and (b) switch between model variants for fallback path.
3) Run staggered short experiments with 4 partner customers (3 days each, low traffic fraction).
4) Capture product KPIs, cost-per-request, and qualitative feedback via SE interviews.

Deliverables:
- Field-lab runbook + experiment configs (Drive link in attachments).
- Dashboard: per-customer latency vs KPI curves and fallback economics (Grafana link).
- Decision memo with recommended default routing/fallback policy and gating criteria for Dedicated contracts.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Runbooks and experiment configs reviewed and signed off by Eng and Legal; 2) Telemetry and dashboards ingest data for all three cohorts; 3) At least 3 partner customers completed experiments and provided SE interviews; 4) Resulting policy matrix and recommended defaults uploaded to the PRD and shared with Console and Optimize teams.
